beats.narration: The cumulative task plants three defects in one deployed accelerator — one per layer of this module: packaging, versioning, and the boundary. If you haven't found and corrected all three, pause. Spoilers from here.

Defect one, packaging: the repo path is hardcoded to one customer's checkout directory, so the next engagement can't configure the asset without editing the loop. The fix is checkpoint one all over again, now in context — lift the path into the function signature and let each engagement pass its own.

elements.code:
repo_path="/home/acme/checkout"    # ✗ one customer
def build_agent(repo_path):        # ✓ parameterized

elements.text: ✓ configure per engagement — never edit the loop

beats.narration: Defect two, versioning: the model is the moving alias, opus, and no prior version is retained. When the alias advances, production changes silently, with nothing to roll back to. The fix: pin the full Bedrock model ID, keep the previous pin as the rollback target, and gate the promotion on the bundled eval beating the pinned baseline.

elements.code:
model="opus"                            # ✗ alias moves
model="us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"    # ✓ pinned
retain_previous_pinned_version=True     # ✓ rollback
assert eval_suite.run(...) >= baseline  # ✓ gate

elements.text: alias advance = silent prod change, no rollback

beats.narration: Defect three, the boundary: fetched content from the code task flows straight into the next call, as instructions. One wrapper closes it — treat as data — so a page that carries instructions gets read, not obeyed. The exact seam the trust-boundaries section marked.

One accelerator, the module in miniature: parameterized, pinned, and bounded — with the eval gating the ship. If you caught all three, you're reviewing deployments the way a customer's auditor will. Next: the final takeaways.
